newsitem.title: UK: Halifax float worth 1,300 stg a head - FT.
newsitem.headline: Halifax float worth 1,300 stg a head - FT.

text.p: The Halifax Building Society's planned conversion into a bank and subsequent stock market float could be worth an average of about 1,300 stg for each of the 8.5 million members of Britain's largest mortgage lending group, the Financial Times said on Thursday.
Halifax has said it plans to release and distribute on Friday details of the build-up to its transfer, including the need for half of its qualifying members to vote for conversion.
The FT based its rough calculation of the average payout on the latest market estimates of a market capitalisation for the group of 11 billion stg.

The FT also speculated on some of the detailed share distribution levels, saying the basic payout to all borrowers and savers who have held accounts with minimum balances for just over two years was likely to be between 800 and 900 stg.

"There will be an additional payout to savers who had between 1,000 stg and 50,000 stg in their accounts... The maximum payout, for someone with 50,000 stg in savings who is also a borrower, will be about 6,000 stg," the paper added.
A specific valuation range for the society by adviser Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is to be included in the document.
